title: Goal setting and decision-making

match.reason: No single bank point teaches both setting clear goals and weighing decision options against those goals; the closest ones cover goals alone or the business plan document and finance, so a new point fits better.

draft.title: Goal setting and decision-making
card: A goal is a result a business wants to reach. A clear goal says what is wanted and by when, such as 'sell 200 coffees a day by the end of March'.
Clear goals give a new business direction. They tell the owner what matters most and let the owner check progress.
A decision is a choice between options. A good decision lists the options and weighs each one against the goals.
An option that looks cheap or easy may not help the goal. The owner picks the option that best moves the business towards its goals.
draft.remember: Set a clear goal first, then choose the option that best serves it.

a.q: Why does a new business owner set a clear goal before making decisions?
opts: It gives a standard to weigh each option against
It removes the need to compare any options
It guarantees that every decision will succeed
It makes the cheapest option the right choice
a.why: A goal gives the owner something to measure options against, so choices point the same way. It does not remove the need to compare options or guarantee success, because a goal only guides the choice.
a.clue: Think about what the owner compares each option with.

b.q: Aisha opens a bakery in Ballarat. Her goal is to build a base of regular local customers within a year. She can pay for a large online advert across Australia or run a loyalty card in her shop. Which choice fits her goal better, and why?
opts: The loyalty card, as it rewards repeat local customers
The online advert, as it reaches the most people
The loyalty card, as it costs less than the online advert
The online advert, as bigger reach suits any new business
b.why: Her goal is regular local customers, and a loyalty card rewards people who come back to her shop. The online advert reaches many people, but most are far away, so it does not serve this goal. Cost alone is not the reason to choose.
b.clue: Check each option against her goal, not against cost or size.

a.best: It gives a standard to weigh each option against

b.best: The loyalty card, as it rewards repeat local customers
